businessType: B2B wholesale marketplace connecting trade buyers with suppliers across several categories. Founded 2019, total raised $40M (Series B 2023). Monetized via a flat ~12% take-rate (commission) on GMV plus optional promotion fees. Current net revenue $7.0M (commission + fees), 30% YoY growth, GMV ~$58M annualized, ~1,400 active sellers.
stage: Net revenue $7.0M, 30% YoY growth. NRR (seller net revenue retention) fell from 108% to 95%. Seller acquisition slowing. The top 8% of sellers generate 61% of GMV, and several large sellers have begun routing repeat buyers to their own direct channels after initial marketplace introduction. Take-rate is a flat ~12% regardless of seller size or order type. Cash runway 24 months.
ownerGoal: Improve seller value proposition and retention, restore NRR above 105%, and slow large-seller disintermediation; reach $12M net revenue within 18 months.
ownerConstraints: Funding constraint: $40M raised, 24-month runway; the next raise is gated on GMV growth and seller retention, so large-seller GMV leakage is strategically dangerous.

Product constraint: the platform can support tiered/volume-based take-rates and value-added services (financing, logistics, buyer analytics) but these require 6-10 weeks of product+billing work to launch.
Organizational constraint: 70 staff (20 engineering, 16 seller-success/account-management, 14 buyer growth, rest G&A); account management covers large sellers but has no pricing-negotiation mandate.

Market constraint: large sellers increasingly have the scale and tooling to run direct buyer relationships once the marketplace has introduced the buyer; small/mid sellers still depend on marketplace demand generation.

Commercial constraint: a flat 12% take-rate is cheap for low-repeat, demand-dependent small sellers but expensive for high-volume, repeat-heavy large sellers whose buyers are now 'sticky' and disintermediable.
immediateConcern: Seller NRR has fallen 108%→95% and the largest sellers, who drive 61% of GMV, are routing repeat buyers off-platform after the first marketplace-sourced order. The owner believes seller satisfaction and the value proposition are declining and wants to invest in seller-success headcount and new seller features. But the data shows the problem is concentrated and structural: the flat 12% take-rate is economically irrational for high-volume repeat sellers, who pay 12% on buyers the marketplace no longer needs to source, giving them a clear incentive to disintermediate. Small/mid sellers, who still depend on demand generation, are not leaving. The owner must decide within the next month whether to add seller-success resources broadly or restructure take-rate/monetization for the large-seller segment before more GMV leaks off-platform.
